question:
What is the area of the shaded figure shown below?

[Figure 1](figures/2021_Fall_AMC_12B_Q02_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The shaded region is the triangle with vertices \((1,0),(3,5),(5,0)\) after removing the inner triangle with vertices \((1,0),(3,2),(5,0)\). Both triangles have the same horizontal base of length \(5-1=4\). Their heights above that base are \(5\) and \(2\), respectively. Therefore the shaded area is
\[
\frac12\cdot4\cdot5-\frac12\cdot4\cdot2
=10-4=\boxed{6}
\]
square units, choice \(\mathrm{B}\).

edges.reason: Perpendicular constructions and uniqueness explain orthogonal projections, but plotting on an existing square grid needs only its given axes. Keep the useful geometry preparation without imposing the full construction workflow.
Each coordinate axis is a number line with an origin, a direction and a unit. Plotting and reading coordinates is impossible without understanding those three elements of a number line.
edges.scope: coordinate axes as two perpendicular number lines

edges.reason: Each axis is a signed number line, so plotting signed coordinates uses number-to-position interpretation on it.
edges.scope: axes as number lines with negatives

edges.reason: A point's two coordinates form an ordered pair; swapping the entries generally changes the point.

Gemini uses quadrant/axis features to assign coordinates in one diagram method. Coordinate differences and area can instead be computed from already supplied points without quadrant classification, so these features prepare rather than universally precede the task.
edges.scope: segment lengths and areas from coordinates

edges.reason: Triangle classification helps recognize where an altitude may lie. The area relation and a supplied base/height can be used across all triangle types without first sorting them as acute, right or obtuse.
edges.scope: locating heights in right and obtuse triangles

edges.reason: The target explicitly states that the triangle has half the area of an equal-base equal-height parallelogram. Parallelogram-area meaning is needed for that specified comparison.

The criterion explicitly permits triangles OR rectangles. Both external reviews turn that alternative into an unconditional requirement, but an L-shaped orthogonal figure can be split entirely into rectangles. Preserve triangle area as a component of the triangular-piece route without making every composite-area task use it.
edges.scope: Calculating triangular pieces in a triangular partition of a composite area
